questions.q: What does reconciling an Order-to-Cash transaction mean?
options: Re-entering the order from scratch
Deleting and recreating the invoice
Confirming that quantity, amount, and status agree at every handoff from order to GL
Only checking the final GL balance, ignoring everything upstream
questions.explain: Reconciliation verifies agreement across the full chain of handoffs, not just a single endpoint.

questions.q: What is SO-48217's credit memo amount, and does it tie to the return quantity?
options: $2,755.00, for 20 returned units at $137.75 each
$5,800.00, for 40 returned units
$2,900.00, for 20 returned units at list price
$0.00, because returns have no accounting effect
questions.explain: 20 returned units x $137.75 net unit price = $2,755.00, which ties cleanly to the return.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does "this order reconciles" actually mean in practice?
options: A single report says "OK" with no further detail needed
The order was entered without any holds
The customer confirmed the order verbally
A chain of individually verifiable facts that are each consistent with their neighboring checkpoint
questions.explain: Reconciliation means each checkpoint is verifiably consistent with the one before and after it, not a single pass/fail flag.

questions.q: In day-to-day practice, who or what typically performs most reconciliation checking?
options: It is always done entirely by hand, line by line, for every order
Oracle Fusion's own reports (aging, reconciliation reports, trial balances) do most of this automatically
The customer's own finance team
It is never done at all
questions.explain: Automated reports handle routine reconciliation; manual checking becomes necessary specifically when something doesn't tie out.

questions.q: When something doesn't reconcile, where does the lesson say the problem is typically located?
options: Spread evenly across every checkpoint at once
Always in the General Ledger, never upstream
At one specific checkpoint in the chain, which the consultant has to isolate
Always in the customer's bank
questions.explain: A broken reconciliation traces to one specific checkpoint in the chain, not an even spread of error across the whole process.
